Usage: wizcli scan dir <path> [flags]

Scan a directory

Arguments:
  <path>    Path to scan

Flags:
  -h, --help    Show context-sensitive help.

Directory scan options
  --disabled-scanners=DISABLED-SCANNERS,...
      Scanners to disable for the scan (Supported:
      Vulnerability,Secret,SensitiveData,Misconfiguration,SoftwareSupplyChain,AIModels,SAST,Malware)

Common scan options
      --client-id=STRING          Wiz service account's client ID
                                  ($WIZ_CLIENT_ID)
      --client-secret=STRING      Wiz service account's client secret
                                  ($WIZ_CLIENT_SECRET)
      --projects=PROJECTS,...     Scopes the scan to specific Wiz Projects
                                  by ID or slug (slug is only supported when
                                  authenticating via a Wiz Deployment with its
                                  auto-generated service account). If not used,
                                  the scan defaults to all Projects associated
                                  with the authenticated service account.
      --use-device-code           Use device code flow for authentication,
                                  ignores client ID and secret
      --no-browser                Do not open browser for device code flow
      --name=STRING               Scan name. If empty, will be auto-generated
                                  based on the scan type and scanned target
      --timeout=1h                Timeout for the scan
  -p, --policies=POLICIES,...     Policies to apply to the scan
      --applications=APPLICATIONS,...
                                  Defines the code application environment; this
                                  affects the applied ignore rules when provided
  -t, --tags=TAGS-VALUE           Tags to mark the scan with, can be KEY or
                                  KEY=VALUE
      --no-publish                Disable publishing scan results to the Wiz
                                  portal
      --wiz-configuration-file=STRING
                                  Path (relative to the current working
                                  directory) to the Wiz configuration file.
                                  Will use .wiz file if not specified
      --scan-context-id=STRING    Context identifier that defines scan
                                  granularity ($WIZ_SCAN_CONTEXT_ID)

Scan output options
  -C, --no-color                   Disable color output
  -S, --no-style                   Disable stylized output
  -T, --no-telemetry               Disable telemetry
      --log=STRING                 File path at which to write debug logs
                                   (defaults to no logs)
      --stdout="human"             Output type for stdout (Supported:
                                   human,json,csv,sarif)
      --sbom-format=STRING         Generate a Software Bill of Materials (SBOM)
                                   report. Available options are [cyclonedx-xml,
                                   cyclonedx-json, spdx-txt, spdx-json]
      --sbom-output-file=STRING    Local file path to store the Software Bill of
                                   Materials (SBOM) report
      --csv-output-file=STRING     Local file path to store the CSV report as a
                                   zip archive
      --sarif-output-file=STRING
                                   Local file path to store the Sarif report
      --json-output-file=STRING    Local file path to store the Json report
      --human-output-file=STRING
                                   Local file path to store the Human report

Scan results filter options
  --by-policy-hits="BLOCK"    Show only results by policy hits (Supported:
                              BLOCK, AUDIT, DISABLED)
  --show-ignored-by-grace-period
                              Show results ignored by grace period even if they
                              are not policy hits

IaC scan options
  --types=all,...                 Narrow down the scan to specific
                                  types (supported values:
                                  Ansible,AzureResourceManager,Bicep,Cloudformation,Crossplane,Dockerfile,GitHubActions,GoogleCloudDeploymentManager,Kubernetes,Pulumi,Terraform)
  --dir-traversal-workers=64      Number of workers used during directory
                                  traversal phase
  --rule-evaluation-workers=64    Number of workers used during rule evaluation
                                  phase
  --max-file-size=64 MiB          Maximum file size to scan, can be specified in
                                  SI units, e.g. 1MiB, 64KiB, 2GB, 1048576
  --discovered-resources          In supported platforms (currently Terraform
                                  only), discover cloud resources and include
                                  them in the scan's JSON output
  --ignore-comments               Enable ignore comments: files, code blocks,
                                  and lines will be ignored
  --expand-cloudformation-intrinsics
                                  Expand intrinsic functions when processing
                                  CloudFormation templates (default:true)
  --max-depth=32                  Maximum depth of intrinsic functions when
                                  evaluating CloudFormation templates
  --keep-false-conditions         When processing CloudFormation templates,
                                  if a Resource object has a Condition field,
                                  and this condition evaluates to false,
                                  we will keep this Resource object and
                                  validate it Default behaviour is to remove
                                  Resource objects with false conditions.
                                  Using this flag automatically enables the
                                  --expand-cloudformation-intrinsics flag
  --tag-file=TAG-FILES-CMD        Comma-seperated 2-tuple in which the first
                                  element is a glob-pattern which expands to
                                  the file paths to apply the external tags to,
                                  and the second element is a glob-pattern which
                                  expands to the file paths of the external
                                  tag files. Each external tag file is a JSON
                                  formatted file that contains a dictionary, in
                                  which a key represents a tag key and the value
                                  represents a tag value (e.g. { "tag_key1":
                                  "tag_value1", "tag_key2": "tag_value2" }).
                                  Using this flag automatically enables the
                                  --expand-cloudformation-intrinsics flag
  --parameter-files=PARAMETER-FILES,...
                                  Comma separated list of globs of external
                                  parameter files to include while scanning.
                                  Using this flag automatically enables the
                                  --expand-cloudformation-intrinsics flag

Vulnerability scan options
  --scan-os-managed-libraries    Enable or disable scanning of OS-package
                                 managed code libraries for this scan (overrides
                                 tenant setting)
  --scan-go-standard-library     Enable or disable scanning of Go Standard
                                 library for this scan (overrides tenant
                                 setting)
  --apply-code-library-exclusion-paths-legacy
                                 Enable or disable applying code library
                                 exclusion paths (legacy) for this scan
                                 (overrides tenant setting)
  --ignore-code-library-vulns-in-redhat-openshift-images
                                 Enable or disable ignoring code library
                                 vulnerabilities in Red Hat Openshift container
                                 images for this scan (overrides tenant setting)
  --scan-sbom                    Scan SBOM files in the scan target (no creator
                                 comment "Installed Packages" is required)
  --scan-python-custom-requirements
                                 Enable or disable scanning of custom Python
                                 requirements files for this scan (overrides
                                 tenant setting)

SAST scan options
  --sast-no-gitignore    Disable respecting .gitignore files during SAST
                         scanning. If this flag is omitted, git must be
                         installed to scan git repositories.
